name: Use the canonical catalog language from the context documents
description: Domain terms live in CONTEXT-MAP.md and docs/contexts/<context>/CONTEXT.md, one glossary per context. Use these terms exactly in code, docs and the UI, and check the glossary before adding a term. Keep the files current with the domain-modeling skill. docs/PRODUCT_PLAN.md was never committed.

title: Keep a CAD item's identity, its stored bytes and its revisions separate
rationale: A CAD item keeps its identity over time. Its stored bytes are identified by their SHA-256, and each revision's hash covers its content and license. Source and license belong to one exact CAD item revision. Moving or copying stored bytes never creates a revision.

title: Keep verification and protection separate
rationale: Verification is permanent proof about one exact revision. Protection is an audited setting that blocks changes to a part or CAD item. To fix a protected item, remove the protection with a reason, revise it, verify the new revision, then protect it again. Authority is never a silent way around protection.

title: Derive Catalog record IDs from content; compare CSV imports on the server
rationale: Each Catalog record ID is the first 15 hex digits of SHA-256('kicad-parts:<kind>:v1\n<key>'), computed in crates/catalog/src/ids.rs and again by the route. So re-imports find the same records. A symbol's blob is the bytes of that one symbol. POST /api/catalog/csv-imports compares with stored state in one transaction. Partly replaced by mx-c5e787 and mx-64c42a.

name: Catalog write guards and tamper tests
description: catalog_write_guards.pb.js refuses every record API write to catalog_* records with 403, superusers included. Server code may only move a part's current pointers forward, or between revisions that aren't archived. New revisions, details, archive entries and reviews must match what their route saves. To test ID collisions, stop the server, edit data.db with rusqlite, and restart.

title: Each CSV import run records what the CSV said
rationale: A run's audit entry records the files read with hashes, every row's bytes, where it left each part, removed parts, and every import problem found. A run is recorded whenever its files differ from the last run, so the latest run holds what the CSV says now. tooling/catalog-import zero_loss.rs rebuilds the CSV from the latest run.

title: CSV imports state expected revisions; older checkouts and uncommitted changes are refused
rationale: ImportCommand carries the current revision and details it expects per part, so the route answers 409 conflict or 409 newer_import_run when state moved. tooling/catalog-import refuses a checkout older than the latest import run, and uncommitted changes to the files the import reads. The overrides, allow_older_checkout and --allow-uncommitted-changes, are recorded on the audit entry.

name: Hash CSV import blobs as UTF-8 text when possible, else in JavaScript
description: $security.sha256 hashes text only, and passing it a Go []byte hashes '72,69,...' instead. Send UTF-8 blobs as text and store toBytes(text), about 50 ms per MiB. Send other bytes as base64, decoded and hashed in catalog_lib.js, about 3 s per MiB. The route allows 32 MiB bodies, and submit_import refuses larger ones first.

name: Catalog hook storage and shared code
description: Store documents whose SHA-256 is their identity in text fields with an explicit max, because a max of 0 means 5000; never use json fields. Load shared hook code from catalog_lib.js with require inside the handler. Values used when registering a route may be top-level consts of the .pb.js file.

title: Extra MPN columns become import problems; BOM exclusion comes from KiCad flags
rationale: Extra manufacturer part number (MPN) columns, MPN TBC and other MPN-like headers never go into part details; non-blank values become import problems. Excluded from BOM is true only when the bound local symbol says (in_bom no), or every footprint choice has exclude_from_bom. The server works it out for every new revision. zero_loss.rs checks these rules.

title: App edits always win over CSV imports; accept differences field by field
rationale: Decided 2026-10-10: a re-import never overwrites an edit. Per part and kind, details follow the CSV only while the current details came from an import, and CAD likewise; otherwise the import records a problem. When the CSV changes after an edit, the app asks the person to accept CSV values field by field (kicad-parts-75a5).

title: Number CAD item revisions like parts; KiCad always gets the current revision
rationale: Decided 2026-10-10. Going back to earlier content adds a new numbered CAD item revision, while bytes are stored once, so the current revision is always the newest. A binding keeps its revision while the CAD content is the same. How KiCad gets revisions is now mx-f75a28. How it works: mx-0a590f.

title: Imports from uncommitted changes are refused unless overridden
rationale: Decided 2026-10-10: commit first, because one rule is easier to explain. An import whose files differ from HEAD is refused before sending, naming the files, unless --allow-uncommitted-changes is given. The audit entry records the override. A later clean run is always recorded, so it replaces the uncommitted one. Details in mx-64c42a.

title: Only CAD changes add revisions; details are shared; archive replaces restore
rationale: Decided 2026-10-10: old products keep their exact parts while new designs use the newest. A part revision is the exact symbol, footprint and 3D model revisions, and only a CAD change adds one. Details and manufacturer parts belong to the IPN and are shared. A bad revision is archived, never deleted. Built in kicad-parts-7556 and kicad-parts-5bea.

name: CAD item revisions are numbered; snapshots name them by number and hash
description: Seed kicad-parts-54d5. A CAD item revision ID is deriveId('cad-item-revision', cad_item + newline + number), and its current revision is the newest number. References carry cad_item, number and snapshot_sha256, so readers can check the record. A binding keeps its revision while the content hash matches the current revision. The route refuses wrong IDs or numbers with 400.

title: Archive rules: never the last revision, and undo needs a reason
rationale: Decided 2026-10-10 (kicad-parts-bd76 plan). A part's last revision that isn't archived can't be archived, so every part has a current revision. Unarchive needs a reason. Only part revisions are archived for now. App edits win over CSV imports per part and kind, and Excluded from BOM is worked out for every new revision.

name: Part details are stored apart from part revisions
description: Seed kicad-parts-7556. catalog_part_details and catalog_part_revisions are immutable, numbered, hashed records per part, and details never hold Symbol or Footprint. Edits send details and CAD as separate sections, each checked against its own number, so a details edit never conflicts with a CAD change. Imports save details or CAD only while the current one came from an import.

name: Archived part revisions
description: Seed kicad-parts-5bea. Archiving adds an append-only catalog_archive_entries record; nothing is deleted or changed. A revision's state is its newest entry, and the part's current revision is its newest one not archived. POST /api/catalog/archives refuses to archive the last such revision. An import never brings archived CAD back; it records csv-cad-matches-archived-revision instead.

name: Reviewing CSV changes on edited parts
description: Seed kicad-parts-75a5. POST /api/catalog/csv-reviews takes accepted field names, and the server builds what it saves from the recorded CSV document. Each review is one csv-review Change. A review covers that CSV text, so the app asks again only when the CSV changes. Problems stay recorded for the zero-loss report.

name: The server works out Excluded from BOM for every new revision
description: Seed kicad-parts-ccc0. The value comes only from KiCad flags in the bound CAD bytes: (in_bom no) on the symbol, or exclude_from_bom on every footprint choice. catalog_lib.js has an s-expression reader that must match library_file.rs byte for byte, and pocketbase_bom.rs tests that. An existing revision never changes, so no old BOM changes.

name: The import state reads only current records
description: Seed kicad-parts-7828. read_import_state reads small fields of current records only, plus bound revisions that aren't current and the latest run per CSV file. The route accepts csvFile only as a plain name, because PocketBase filters undo only quote escapes. An index on predecessor keeps the newest-revision filter fast: 0.19 s at 6,000 revisions.

title: Guess a new part's category from layered clues the team confirms
rationale: Decided 2026-10-11 (kicad-parts-9693, kicad-parts-ae44). Descriptions alone guess poorly. Clues, most reliable first: confirmed matches and known MPNs, footprint name, symbol reference letter, nearest existing parts, then supplier categories. Preselect the best guess with its reason and two alternatives; the engineer always confirms. It works offline and deterministically, with no AI service.

title: The CSV catalog groups footprints by package and team symbols by category
rationale: kicad-parts-82ea, a one-time regroup the user approved. Footprints live in footprints/g-<KiCad footprint library>.pretty, such as g-Resistor_SMD. 3D models live in 3d-models/g-<footprint library>.3dshapes/<footprint name>.step. Team symbols are split by category, such as g-res and g-cap. The full old-to-new mapping is in the regroup commit's message.

title: CSV CAD is kept and flagged; app edits are strict
rationale: QA review 2026-10-12. A CSV row naming several symbols, or repeating a footprint choice, imports as written with an import problem. The edit route refuses to make either, but only when the edit changes that value, so an old CSV slip never blocks an unrelated edit. A CSV review may still accept such CAD.

name: Edits that upload CAD files
description: Seed kicad-parts-3b8b. POST /api/catalog/edits takes cad.uploads, and the server reads every file itself with the BOM marks' s-expression reader. Symbols and footprints must be UTF-8 text with names matching their reference; 3D models may be base64. Content equal to the current revision adds nothing; other content adds a revision. Bad files get 400, and nothing is written.

title: A CSV import never replaces CAD made in the app
rationale: Seed kicad-parts-3b8b. A CAD item is made in the app while its current revision's Change isn't a csv-import. Imports never send such items, and bind parts to the last imported revision. If the CSV's content differs, each part using it gets csv-cad-differs-from-edited-cad-item, which a review can only keep. Storing the CSV file would replace the app's revision for KiCad.

name: Review fixes to edits with files: name rules, caught-up CSV, batched reads
description: Seed kicad-parts-3b8b review. Names from chosen files reach the filesystem, so they must be plain: no control characters and no leading '-', checked in Rust and catalog_lib.js. 3D model keys must be 3d-models/g-<library>.3dshapes/<file>. A CSV is unchanged for app-made CAD when it equals either the last imported or the current revision.

content: Edit part uploads bind only 3D models at 3d-models/g-<footprint library>.3dshapes/<file>; other Catalog model paths are saved as missing. The CSV import is looser, but every current CSV model is already in g-*.3dshapes. If the import ever meets a model elsewhere, move the model instead of loosening the upload rule.

name: Categories, a part's category and remembered matches
description: Seed kicad-parts-ae44: migration 1792300000_categories.js adds catalog_categories, numbered category revisions and catalog_category_matches. Part details schema 3 holds a category code. Changing a part's category in an edit adds the new category's missing fields and saves one remembered match per clue. Imports and CSV reviews never make matches. zero_loss.rs checks each part's category.

title: Category calls made by best judgement in kicad-parts-ae44
rationale: Spec 2026-10-11 left these open: an import takes only a stored category's fields and keeps its name, prefix and rules. Category changes never drop fields. A CSV review that accepts Category makes no remembered match. The server works out matches, and clients never send them. Category history has no screen yet (kicad-parts-5514).

name: Category guess engine and its leave-one-out accuracy on the CSV catalog
description: crates/catalog/src/guess.rs ranks every category with integer points, strongest first: same MPN 1000, remembered matches up to 150, footprint pattern 100, reference letter 60, keywords, then the 5 nearest parts. Leave-one-out on 178 parts: top-1 88.2%, top-3 98.9%. Weak categories: cpd, mpu, pwr, rfm and pcb. Some keywords were written with the catalog in view, so new parts may do worse.

name: Adding a new part from downloaded CAD files
description: Seed kicad-parts-9693. POST /api/catalog/parts saves one Change of kind create with the part, details 1, revision 1 and any new CAD item revisions. A file whose CAD item exists with other content is refused, so a new part never changes other parts. crates/catalog download.rs reads vendor ZIPs with size limits. An IPN the Catalog has gets 409 ipn_taken.

title: Add part calls made by best judgement in kicad-parts-9693
rationale: Spec 2026-10-12 left these open: Add part sits beside Search parts, for editors only. A new Change kind, create, makes history say Added. The next free IPN is the prefix's highest middle number plus 1, with variant 0001. The footprint links to the download's 3D model at save time. IPN-taken answers aren't stored, so a retry is checked again.

name: Review fixes to Add part
description: Seed kicad-parts-9693 review. Sexp::parse refuses nesting deeper than 256, because a hostile footprint overflowed the stack. The server refuses an IPN whose prefix isn't the category's. ipn_taken says when you added the part yourself, so a lost answer can't add it twice. The form keeps typed values across re-reads and checks the MPN after 300 ms.

name: QA pass 2: cross-feature fixes to Add part, CSV reviews and conflicts
description: QA 2026-10-12, corrected by mx-a54532. Add part sends a download's file only when the reference names that file in a g- library. Requests over 32 MiB get a note to choose a smaller 3D model. A CSV review can't accept CAD the CSV lacks while the Catalog has it. Two editors replacing one footprint with different files now conflict.

content: Edits are sent in two sections, details and CAD, each with the number it started from; a file in Edit part plus someone else's details change merge without a conflict. Only a change to the same section conflicts, and a chosen file must show as a conflict row of its own, because its reference text usually stays the same.

Add part leaves a download's file out only when the reference names another item after the colon. The file's own name in a non-g library, or with no library, keeps the file, so check_name refuses it plainly. Model file names have " < > | ? * replaced by _ before the key is built.

title: Hand-made KiCad CAD stays supported; a library check finds it
rationale: Decided 2026-10-12 (kicad-parts-da65, kicad-parts-37a7). Engineers may still draw symbols and footprints in our g- libraries. A library check, shared by the import and the desktop, warns about items no part uses and checks each footprint's 3D model link. Bad links on new or changed footprints stop the import. Today's CSV catalog files stay as they are.

title: Library check calls made by best judgement in kicad-parts-da65
rationale: Spec 2026-10-12 left these open; calls 1 and 8 are replaced by mx-c05d31. 'Since the last import' is per CSV file. Only errors in files the import reads stop it, with no override flag. The pilot prints the check to stderr. The desktop shows a line under the search box that opens the check in the part panel.

name: The library check: one pure function for the import and the desktop
description: Seed kicad-parts-da65. check() in crates/catalog/src/library_check/mod.rs takes the libraries, known CAD, CSV references and KiCad footprints, and returns sorted findings: To fix, Clean-up, Not in the Catalog yet, or Worth a look. read.rs reads the folders. The import calls it in prepare_checked_import, and the desktop caches it per editor position. Journey 14 covers the view.

title: Library check review: today's footprints exempt; server checks model links
rationale: Review 2026-10-12, replacing calls 1 and 8 of mx-7bf4ef. A footprint keeps old problems as clean-up only while its bytes equal today's CSV catalog's. The team server refuses an uploaded footprint whose model link points outside ${GITPLM_PARTS}/3d-models. The desktop cache key adds a folder fingerprint. Unreadable files and links become findings, not failures.

title: Library check re-review: frozen baseline, today's CSV files, unquoted model paths
rationale: Re-review 2026-10-13, refining mx-c05d31. The first-import exception also needs every CSV file using the footprint to be one of today's 21. The baseline is a checked-in constant in library_check/today.rs; when the fixture moves, change the test, not the list. Unquoted KiCad 5 model paths are judged too.

title: Add part from our libraries calls made by best judgement in kicad-parts-37a7
rationale: Spec 2026-10-12 left these open. Every file to send must be committed exactly as it is, with no override. The picker offers library items not yet in the Catalog. The footprint's bytes are never rewritten, so a later CSV import finds the same bytes. Library check errors, outside or missing model links, and uncommitted files stop the save.

name: Add part from symbols and footprints already in our libraries
description: Seed kicad-parts-37a7. catalog-browser library_part.rs reads the chosen symbol and footprint, checks them with the library check, and confirms git holds their bytes. Uploads carry a library source with path, file hash, commit and symbol byte range, the CSV import's source shape. So a later import of the same items with the same bytes changes nothing. Journey 15 covers it.

title: Add part review: revisions from our libraries count as imported
rationale: Review 2026-10-13. A CAD item revision with source 'library' holds the CSV catalog's own file, so it's an import base, not app-made CAD. Redrawing it in KiCad and importing adds a revision with no false notice. The commit check hashes the bytes already read, so a later KiCad save can't be sent as committed.

title: Choosing CAD calls made by best judgement in kicad-parts-bc6f
rationale: Spec 2026-10-13 left these open. Our items the Catalog lacks are found by reference at save, with no request field. A copied footprint maps to the choice named like it. A drawing shows only what changed; the part's own stays left. With a download, another chosen symbol keeps what the download said.

content: A copy from an installed library is an upload with an installed Source (nickname and path), never library. Imports then treat it as app CAD. Readable outside 3D models are copied to g-<lib>.3dshapes and relinked; unreadable ones stop the save unless No 3D model. See crates/catalog-browser/src/pick.rs.
